fields.title: Polka: a supplier that stopped responding
fields.summary: An hour of slow responses from someone else's API brought down the whole app. Two more chains are connecting.
fields.decisionPrompt: How do we build work with partner catalogs?
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a customer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a Polka PM. The Domashniy chain catalog—40 stores, 12 thousand items—comes from their system via API. Yesterday, their API took 40 seconds to respond instead of one second for an hour, and the Polka app stopped opening entirely for all users. The incident was analyzed, the question is what to do next. Two more chains with their own APIs are connecting.
fields.brief/objective: Ensure a partner API failure does not take down the entire product.
fields.brief/constraints: Their SLA is 99% availability and no speed obligations. No leverage in negotiations.
fields.brief/task: Decide how you build work with partner catalogs and what you do on day one.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Someone else's system will go down—the question is what goes down with it
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Integration without a timeout turns someone else's slowness into your own outage: requests pile up and take down the entire product. A timeout costs hours of work and is set first. Then cache solves availability, but every field has its own staleness price: prices can be shown from yesterday, stock levels cannot, so they are requested at the moment an error costs money.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: The chain catalog is requested when opening the store screen, directly, without cache. No timeout on the call.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: "Without a timeout, requests piled up, the connection pool exhausted, all app requests froze, including those unrelated to this chain. Timeout takes an hour of work. Export cache takes a week. They have no webhooks, only a full export: 12 thousand items, 100 per request, 30 requests per minute—4 minutes."
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: 99% availability, which means up to 7 hours of downtime per month. No response speed obligations.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Chain prices change twice a day, usually at night. Stock levels change constantly.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Day and a half. 3-second timeout, upon failure the chain's stores are marked temporarily unavailable, the rest of the app works.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: eliminates catastrophe—one chain going down no longer brings down the product. But 18% of turnover is unavailable for the entire duration of the outage, up to 7 hours a month per their SLA.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: A week and a half. The catalog is exported once an hour in the background and stored with us; the screen reads our cache, not their API.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: their API failure is unnoticeable to the buyer for up to a day. Prices may lag by an hour—with changes twice a day this is acceptable. Stock levels lag by an hour, which is already a problem: someone will add an out-of-stock item. Requires a separate solution for stock.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Catalog cache plus stock check at checkout
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Two and a half weeks. Catalog from cache, stock requested from the chain only at checkout, with a timeout and plan B.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: covers both availability and accuracy where it's critical. More expensive in time. If their API is down at checkout—an honest refusal for specific items, not the whole app.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Demand webhooks and speed SLAs from partners
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Demand webhooks and speed SLAs from partners. Negotiations, timeframe unknown.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: right in substance and solves nothing in the quarter horizon. Domashniy has no leverage—they are bigger than us in these negotiations. For two connecting chains, this can become part of the conditions.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not understand the danger of a slow response
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not read API limits as a product constraint
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not distinguish freshness requirements for different data
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Synchronous call to someone else's system is not separated from own user path
